## Mask of relentless compassion

Mask of relentless compassion was an enchanted masked cowl that boosted the wearer's healing magic in exchange for draining their damage-dealing potential, created sometime before the late 15 century DR.

Powers
These cloth masks boosted the wearer's wisdom and doubled their healing magic's potency, in exchange for taking away all of their offensive capabilities. It also was a cursed item, rendering the wearer unable to deal more than a harmless scratch worth of damage, compelled to perform good deeds, and unable to peel the mask off their face.

History
These cursed items were originally designed to be worn by individuals looking to conceal their true intentions behind a mask of benevolence and righteousness. Some thought that the curse that compelled the wearer to do good deeds was added to the item as a way to punish someone.

In the late 15 century DR, the mask was sold to Perren a malicious drow from the area of Underdark under the Savage Frontier in northwest Faerûn. Cursed with being good and unable to attacks anyone nor anything, Perren resorted to begging for help. The Champion of the Burning Dawn and their allies traveled to Strumoru's Oddities in the Darklake district of Gracklstugh in order to track down the item's seller. Subsequently, the Champion helped Perren to break the mask's curse, freeing the drow from the tyranny of good. As a reward, the heroes received the mask of relentless compassion, now freely usable without the danger of being cursed.

## Maisby

Maisby was a human cook and houseservant who lived near Eveningstar in Cormyr during the mid-1480s DR.

Description

Maisby had shoulder-length brown hair, brown eyes, and a light skin tone. She typically wore a neat black and white short dress and leggings.

History

Around the time of the Sschindylryn invasion of Eveningstar, Maisby worked as a cook at the Midler farmstead, a large home west of Eveningstar. When the drow attacked in force, Maisby managed to escape the attention of the cruel priestess of Lolth Vicala Szind by hiding in the shed behind the home. She waited there for a night and a day, then slipped away back to Eveningstar. There, she reported what had happened, including that the Midler family had actually been taken alive and kept as hostages, rather than killed. The Evenor Helena Falagon took care of the distraught Maisby while Vicben Arroway and another Purple Dragon investigated, but they did not return. Following that, a team of adventurers were sent in to rescue the Midlers.

Later, Maisby found work as a housemaid at the mysterious Sable Manor, alongside Saunders, Willem, and Scraps. She was fortunately not immediately targeted by the villainous vampire Lord Sable when he made his return only a few days after her arrival, with Sir Ebermund Harker and the other guests suffering instead. Instead, she was kept busy cleaning and maintaining the mansion while dark deeds were performed in the background.

## Masthead of durability

A masthead of durability was a type of enchanted mast step that vastly improved the durability of any mast that was installed into it. They were primarily used in Realmspace among spelljammers.This item is a "masthead" in name only. A masthead is defined as being the top part of a mast, whilst this item is consistently described across sources as being the "lower support for a mast". The more appropriate term for such a structural component would be a "mast step", something that's located at the base of a mast and designed to support its weight and secure it to a deck.

Description
These small silver items were structural supports installed at the base of masts, physically bolting them to their decks.

Powers
Any mast that was equipped with a masthead of durability would be vastly strengthened, becoming virtually indestructible to physical attacks. Additionally, if a spelljammer were to ever attempt shearing off the top of a mast, the ship would suffer damage equivalent to its tonnage. However, they could not protect masts against destruction by fire.

## Mask of beastliness

A mask of beastliness was a magical mask created by barbarians that allowed the wearer to temporarily transform their head into that of a beast.

Description
Masks of beastliness were carved from wood in the likeness of a beast's visage, though with grotesquely exaggerated features, and colored in various dyes. They had eye slits to see through, holes in the creature's nose to breath through, and leather straps for a wearer to secure it around their head. The animals these masks were most commonly carved to resemble included buffalo, cobras, lions, ravens, rhinoceri, and wild stags.

Powers
Pressing a mask of beastliness against a wearer's face for five consecutive minutes would cause it to fuse with the wearer's flesh and animate, transforming the wearer's head into that of the animal the mask was carved to resemble. This enabled a wearer to inflict greater harm upon their opponents or even inflict poison if their beast had such power, like that of a cobra. However, whilst a mask was active, its wearer was incapable of eating, speaking, or casting spells that required verbal components.

The effects of a mask of beastliness lasted for one hour and could only be activated once per day. To deactivate a mask, one simply had to slip their fingers under the chin area and push the mask away from the wearer's face.

History
Sometime in the mid–14 century DR, a group of adventurers in Ravens Bluff found themselves magically transported by a painting to the land of Chult when searching for Cuthbert Maguluty. In order to return home, they had to retrieve a magical painting depicting Rupertyna Phyneus-Maguluty's cottage that had been stolen by ptera-men. While at the village of the ptera-men, the adventurers found a small treasure hoard within the hut of their chieftain, containing such items as a mask of beastliness, ten spirit arrows, sixteen emeralds, and a dagger with a solid emerald pommel.

## Marshal

Marshal were honorable, martial leaders and tacticians from all walks of life. They were considered by many in the Realms to be an essential facet of an army.

Activities
Many marshals lived rather mercenary lives, hiring out for commission the strategic services of themselves and any forces they commanded. They could often be found traveling in the midst of armies or as part of adventuring companies. Most felt honor bound to fulfill any commission they undertook, but would not sacrifice the lives of the people they commanded – in such circumstances, they would rather choose to end their contract and find a new patron for their compatriots elsewhere.

The types of commissions that a marshal took on were generally reflective of their alignment. Good-aligned were often crusading types, seeking out evil to eradicate, whilst evil-aligned marshals tended to accept commissions that put them in invading and plundering forces. Those of a Lawful bent tended to accept commissions that involved the repelling of such foreign aggressors, while those of a chaotic bent were often found in proper mercenary companies.

Culture
All marshals in the Realms had significant military experience, with some being also fighters or paladins. Some marshals underwent some form of formal training and study to acquire their marked skills in leadership and battle strategy, usually in the army of a noble or within a military academy or war college. There existed several such colleges across the Realms, such as the Academy of Arms in Athkatla. Others started their lives as mere grunts footsoldiers, working their way up the ranks of an army and acquiring experience over time. The decision to undertake this profession sometimes grew from a want to follow in the footsteps of a parent that had served as an officer in an army or mercenary company.

In Cormyr, marshals could be found amongst the ranks of the Purple Dragon knights, where they often had to learn how to coordinate magical strategies alongside conventional military strategies as they worked alongside Cormyr's War Wizards.

Marshals viewed themselves and other marshals as being part of a select class in society, to the point that even a marshal on the opposing side was afforded some respect.

Abilities
While all marshals had basic training in fighting and general knowledge of various forms of armor and weaponry, though lacked any proficiency with tower shields, making them passable warriors, their real strength lied in their ability to command and inspire trust in others. They also tended to be very geographically oriented, having great mental maps of the battlefields or dungeon warrens they treaded. Marshals that had acquired significant experience in their lifetime of commanding others were found to exude a commanding aura through their confidence, making those who fought under them do markedly better within conflicts. In some cases, this commanding aura was even found to improve spellcasting abilities.

Notable Marshals
 Forthar Helvenstron, a marshal who served as commander under the Zhentilar during their invasion of Shadowdale in 1375 DR.
 Rolbanyion Zelnar, an instructor at the Academy of Arms.

## Matter agitation

Matter agitation, originally known as molecular agitation, was a minor psionic devotion of the psychokinesis discipline that allowed a manifester to rapidly excite the molecules within an object so as to generate heat within the target.In 1 edition, it was stated within the "Area of Effect" for molecular agitation that the target could be either an item or a creature, though its description made mention of only items. When the power was updated for 2 edition AD&D, its "Area of Effect" was updated to mention only items, even specifying a target weight of, though the mentions of skin and hair in the effects section implies that it might be possible to target creatures.

Effects
This power could be used to target one item, weighing no more than, within  of the psion. Early instances of this power found that all effects occurred after a period of ten minutes. Later documentation found that molecular agitation's effects were actually evident as early as one minute, but that their severity increased the longer the power was active for.

For the first minute of active use: readily flammable material would ignite and burn brightly, such as paper, parchment, straw, dry grass, etc. Skin would become red and tender. And wood would darken.

After two minutes of active use: wood would begin to smoke and smolder, metal would become hot to the touch (an effect some described as being similar to the spell heat metal), skin would begin to blister, hair would begin to smolder, paint would shrivel, and water would boil.

After three minutes of active use: wood would properly become aflame, metal would be scorching, skin would be burning away, water would be boiling, and lead would melt.

After four minutes, molecular agitation would cause even steel to grow soft, and after five minutes of active use steel would melt.

Display
When used this power manifested an auditory and material display.

Significance
This power was one of the prerequisites for learning the psychokinesis discipline detonate.

Users
This power was knowable by psions and wilders, ardents and divine minds who followed the chaos mantle, and could be gained as a wild talent.

Molecular agitation was exhibited as an innate psionic ability by amethyst dragons, aratha, beljuril dragons, greater shedu, and lythlyx.

In psionics terms, it could be known by duergar,The creatures filed under "in psionics terms" are those who were first stated out with magical powers and rules, which in some cases were described as 'psionics' in fluff text, and then later got stated or revised with actual psionics powers and rules once The Complete Psionics Handbook came out. It also refers to any creatures where psionics were noted in 1 edition, but not carried over as part of their identity into later editions. phoenixes, and planetars.

Thonots, psionic equivalents of shamans within quaggoth society, possessed molecular agitation as one of their psionic powers.

Known/Notable Users
 K'yorl Odran, a drow psionicist and the matron mother of House Oblodra.

## Mantorra Daramos

Mantorra Daramos, better known by her alias Mantorra Hennaflame, was a Thayan invoker active in the city of Bezantur as of mid-to-late 14 century DR.

Description
She was a plain-looking young woman possessing a natural skill for arcane magic.

Personality
Mantorra acted like a spoiled brat: she was self-centered, detested those of lower rank, and was prone to be cruel to people who annoyed or or to toy with people she found amusing. However, she was neither power-hungry nor wholly evil, and possessed the capacity to grow and mature beyond the cruel tendencies she had internalized as a member of the Thayan elite. She was motivated to live an interesting life and to make a name for herself without resting on the laurels of her noble family name, however she was also unafraid to use or manipulate familial connections if needed. She had little interest in political intrigue, and thus did not actively aspire toward becoming a full member of the Red Wizards despite her passion and aptitude for magecraft.

Although she was ostensibly a devotee of Kossuth, the god of fire, she had little interest in the faith except as a diversion from an otherwise boring life. She did, however, find flames and fire to be mesmerizing, and would spend hours gazing into fires as she contemplated humanity.

Relationships
Her family, the Daramos, was a relatively new member of the Thayan nobility founded by her father, Milsantos Daramos, who was the Tharchion of Thazalhar.
She was Milsantos's only daughter, and while she made great use of her family's connections to establish herself, she subsequently avoided using her family name and instead preferred to use the surname "Hennaflame".

The main connection she made using her father's influence was to become the apprentice of Aznar Thrul, the Tharchion of the Priador and the Zulkir of Evocation. From this position, she subsequently was inducted into the Order of Crimson Warlocks by Eternal Flame Mythalanir, head of the Flaming Brazier temple.

History
The young Mantorra found life as Aznar Thrul's apprentice to be boring. By, she had joined the Order of Crimson Warlocks to seek more interesting diversions, and had begun to spend more and more time at the Flaming Brazier temple.

## Madam Ivydanya's Fortunes Revealed

Madam Ivydanya's Fortunes Revealed was a fortune teller shop in the Lower Port in Skullport.

Structure
Madam Ivydanya's Fortunes Revealed was a modest two-story apartment.

Services
Madame Iyvdanya attracted a steady clientele of sailors and pirates, who were known for their superstitions regarding fate and omens. Her divination services included palm readings, tea-leaf readings, and card readings, all priced between 10 sp and 5 gp, depending on her assessment of the client's wealth. Madame Iyvdanya might also use oracle sticks or interpret the patterns formed by melted candle wax. In addition to her priestly abilities, she possessed psionic talents—such as aura sight, object reading, and precognition.

When Madame Iyvdanya foresaw ill fortune, a frequent occurrence in her readings, she advised her clients to follow folk remedies in an attempt to ward off the misfortune. Typical recommendations included wearing clothes inside out for a tenday. For particularly dire predictions, she might direct clients to the Sisters Three Waxworks to purchase a good luck charm or offer one herself, marked with the symbol of Tymora, for 10 gold pieces. These charms were sourced through a partnership with Ramora’s Guile Shipping, which supplied them from Waterdeep. Madame Iyvdanya’s reputation as a fortune-teller was well-regarded in Skullport, especially among those who valued her guidance in matters of fate and protection.

## Magelords of Mintar

The Magelords of Mintar were a cabal of wizards in the city of Mintar that came to rule over the city-state as a magocracy from the early 1 to early 2 century DR.

Activities
The primary interest of the Magelords was the creation magical hybrid creatures, often by means of breeding monsters with their domestic servants and livestock, so that they could produce ever-more-powerful guards and beasts of burden.

History
Over the course of their existence the Magelords of Mintar vied for power within the shadows of the Mintaran government. This all changed in the, when a Rage of Dragons brought the blue great wyrm Iryklathagra to attack the city-state. She battled with its defenders for nearly a month before returning to her lair, leaving the city in ruins and many local ships sunk. This would kick off the Eighth Age of Calimshan. Many of the Magelords died in the conflict, but those who remained arose among the devastation left by Iryklathagra to install themselves as Mintar's new leaders, promising to protect the populace against any further attacks by dragons. Over the course of the next century, the Magelords would work towards exacting vengeance against Iryklathagra. Eventually, in the early 2 century DR, they would manage to ascertain the site of the blue dragon's lair through the use of magical divinations, but their organization would perish before they could make use of the intel.

Around the early 2 century DR, time a number of Calishite merchants hired the Magelords of Mintar to eliminate the Harpers from south Faerûn, as that group's efforts to improve the safety of overland trade-routes were harming rich interests in the nation of Calimshan. At that time the only safe method of getting goods from the Sea of Fallen Stars to the Sword Coast was by traveling through the Vilhon Reach to the Golden Road, thence to ports on the Lake of Steam where the ships that sailed out belonged to Calishite interests. Additionally, some of the brigands that the Harpers were slaying had been sponsored by Calishites, as part of an effort to make competing overland travel perilous. The brigands would often destroy or steal items, which in turn would benefit the Calishites as the only method of replacing said items would be to conduct further trade with the South.

In need of some extra funds for the stock in their hybrid experiments, as well as viewing the Harpers as an attractive source of subjects to experiment on, the Magelords of Mintar agreed to the contract. They sporadically worked to capture or slay Harpers, though on ocassion mistook hired agents of Nathglaryst for members. Nathglaryst, queen of the drow city of Undraeth beneath Turmish, was at the time in a heated conflict with the Harpers over their repeated efforts to free the slaves that were being traded to her. Eventually things heated to the point where the Harpers raised a mercenary army to invade Undraeth circa .

Anticipating that the Magelords of Mintar would use their conflict with Undraeth as an opportunity to strike at them, Khelben Arunsun and his compatriot Elminster made sure that all of the wizard members of the Harpers would be present for the invasion. On the day of attack, the assembled wizards used explosive spells to collapse Undraeth's mineshaft surface-link as the drow were scrambling up from the Underdark to confront them.

The Magelords of Mintar, overconfidently viewing the amassed army as fodder for the taking and having no inkling of how powerful Elminster and Khelben truly were, launched an attack upon them. Prepared for them, the Harpers engaged the Magelords directly in a spell-battle that ravaged miles of the Turmish coast. Many members of the Harpers would perish in the conflict, however, the Magelords would ultimately be the ones to lose the conflict. Only two members of the organization would manage to escape with their lives, Gloran Galleos and Sardukh.

With the Magelords of Mintar defeated, their city-state would fall into chaos. Admist the panic, the information the Magelords had amassed about Iryklathagra would be stolen by a thieves' guild known as the Skeletal Finger.

In the 14 century DR, the lingering memory of the Magelords acted as a namesake to the inn of Magelords' Rest in the city-state they had once ruled.

Members

## Maldur Breakstone

Maldur Breakstone was a human wizard in the service of the gold dragon king Orchtrien of Dawnfire during the Time of Dragons in the 26 millennium before Dalereckoning.

Description
He was burly, with a florid face, and long hair dyed white.

Personality
Maldur considered race a foremost preoccupation, and believed that elves did not value human life. He was also vindictive and scheming, taking constant stock of the perceived weaknesses of his rivals and delighting in their suffering.

Abilities
Maldur Breakstone was a wizard. Among his many spells were one that created a striking fist made of force, one that invoked storm forces to strike with lightning and roaring thunder both, one that sent forth deadly shafts of shadow that caused terror in those whom they struck, and one that radiated bolts of light from him to a great distance away. Another of his spells made his palms sprout fanged mouths. Finally, one of his spells created a scarlet radiance that broke other magics, though it was not clear whether he used all that magic under his own power or if it came from his possessions. He could also cause blinding flashes or explosions, one of which or both came from a wand.

Possessions
He had numerous amulets and enchanted rings. Of note, he carried an ivory wand that caused either blinding flashes or explosions, perhaps both.

Activities
He was a wizard in the court of Dawnfire, serving as a deputy for the King.

Relationships
He served King Orchtrien, and was a rival to fellow wizard and royal deputy Rhespen Ash.

History
Maldur Breakstone had been a rival of Rhespen Ash for years. Maldur pushed King Orchtrien to rule in ways favorable to humans, in direct opposition to Rhespen's preferred policies.

After the rebellion of the three elven clans, Starfall, Vilirith, and Duskmere in, which Prince Bexendral put down, Maldur counseled King Orchtrien that the entire clans be put to the sword right away; the King instead took the advice of his rival, Rhespen Ash, to be more merciful. The heirs of the clans were taken to Dawnfire, where they would be educated, and serve as hostages at the same time.

During a dinner revel celebrating Orchtrien's victory over the red triumvirate, the King asked one of the hostages, Lady Winterflower Duskmere, to sing for him. She sang a ballad about a mad king bringing forth ruin, which Maldur took as an opportunity to chastise her, using a spell to strike her with a fist made of force. He accused her of maligning the king with her song; Rhespen Ash, his rival, defended the Lady. King Orchtrien bid them duel, for he considered their rivalry had gone on long enough. Maldur was defeated in that duel. By the King's command, Maldur made an attempt to work harmoniously with Rhespen since.

Later the same year, after Rhespen Ash returned from winter incursions against the neighboring lands of the green cabal, his forces were met on the path to Dawnfire by Maldur Breakstone, who brought them fresh horses and garments in advance of the celebration in Rhespen's honor. This made Rhespen quite suspicious, owing to Maldur's rank and the trivialness of the task. Maldur also informed Rhespen that the King had taken Winterflower Duskmere as his lover, to forestall any awkwardness. He took pleasure in breaking the bad news to his rival, who had fallen for her.

After the party, Maldur noticed Rhespen was missing much of the time, and tired throughout the day. He spent the next few months anticipating that Rhespen would try to meet in secret with Winterflower. He eventually succeeded in catching him visiting the Lady, only to discover that the elven wizard had transcribed the King's books of magic. With the aid of several half-dragon crossbowmen, Maldur managed to subdue Rhespen, but Winterflower stole the elf's staff, the copied spellbooks, and escaped.

Maldur later took part in the search for the King's spellbooks. He commanded some of the forces that attacked the Duskmere family stronghold.

## Martine (Golden Legion)

Martine was the daughter of Bishou Domincus, a cleric of Helm. She accompanied the Golden Legion in their expedition in 1361 DR that found Maztica. Her capture and death at the hands of the natives provoked the start of a conflict that led to the Legion conquering Ulatos.

Appearance
She had red hair.

Life

She was in Murann with the legion in 1361 DR when they disembarked. She sang the anthem of the legion at the ceremony on shore before they departed and went with her father on the Legion's flagship the Falcon.

When the expedition came to the Green Sisters archipelago, Martine disembarked and walked with Halloran, an officer in the Legion, on the island. While they were together, they were attacked by a Dragonne, but Halloran and several other legionnaires fought it off. Her father was gifted with a slave by the locals, and Martine was disgusted by this, claiming that Helm did not permit slavery, and decided that she would travel on the Osprey, the ship that Halloran was travelling in.

The expedition arrived on continental Maztica near the city of Ulatos. Martine insisted on going with Halloran when they disembarked. He protested, fearing that it might be dangerous, but she nevertheless went with him.

Mixtal, a local cleric of Zaltec had been hunting for a girl named Erixitl in order to sacrifice her to his god. Erixitl had escaped from his custody with the help of the Couatl Chitikas. In order to trick Mixtal, Chitikas used magic to cause Mixtal to perceive Martine to be Erixitl. Mixtal and a large group of Payit warriors came upon Halloran, Martine and several of the other legionnaires in the forest, and Mixtal then attacked in order to capture Martine, whom he thought was Erixitl. Although some of the warriors tried to stop him, since they could clearly see this strange red-haired woman was not Erixitl, Mixtal would not relent and brought Martine with Halloran to the top of a nearby pyramid. He cut out her heart and sacrificed her to Zaltec in the sight of Halloran.

These events then led to a large battle between the Legion and the Payit, which ended with the Legion conquering Ulatos. Following her death, her father also blamed both Halloran for failing to protect her and the natives collectively for sacrificing her. His preaching became filled with talk of Helm's vengeance against transgressors, and he saw all Mazticans as transgressors.

## Markus Cymrych

Markus Cymrych was High King of the Moonshae Isles in the early-to-mid 4 century DR.

Relationships
He was a member of the Cymrych Dynasty and the second son of a former High King, the infamous Gwylloch Cymrych, as well as the younger brother of the legendarily cruel Prince Ketheryll. He was the nephew of his predecessor, High King Gorham.

History
Markus was only eleven years old in the, when both his High King father and his older brother killed themselves and their retainers in a madness-induced melee at the Castle of Skulls. At that time, the crown passed to his father's younger brother, Gorham. Markus would assume the throne of the High King in the, after killing Gorham.

He ruled for eleven years before he died in combat without an apparent heir in the . The throne thus passed to a cousin, Cameron Cymrych, who was the grandson of Markus's great-grandfather.

## Maggie Ni Chuirc

Maggie Ni Chuirc, sister to Aideen Ni Chuirc, was a member of the Dead Eyes, a criminal group from the Lower City that named itself for the grim trophies they collected from the enemies in the late 15 century DR.

Description
Maggie was a human woman with a light skin. She wore a helmet and a set of mundane chainmail armor. In battle, the wielded a spear and a tower shield adorned with the insignia of the Flaming Fist.

History
In the, the Dead Eyes set out to perform a job that would end up setting the gang against the Guild and its leader, Ninefingers. Maggie's sister, Aideen, worked with a local criminal not affiliated with the Guild, Brinks, to pull the heist off. The Guild did not take competition lightly and sent thugs to take care of the Dead Eyes. Her band survived and relocated to a new lair. Unbeknownst to Aideen, one of her men was a traitor. Bard Hiero Lue uncovered the secret stash where Aideen hid the loot, including the Guild's coin, and sent a note to Ninefingers, informing the Guild of the Dead Eyes' lair and the hidden stash's location. The hiding spot was unknown to even Aideen's own sister, which made Maggie furious when she discovered the bard found out her sister's secret. Maggie wanted to kill the bard but reported him to Aideen, who, in turn, stated that once the job was done, she would end Hiero Lue herself. Maggie did not like the idea of keeping the bard alive that long but conceded that her sister knew better as the group's leader. It was unknown if Maggie and the Dead Eyes survived an attack from the Guild or other eager adventurers of Baldur's Gate.

## Malika Tahoun

Malika Tahoun was an oinoloth who was sent to destroy Cube 1717. There, it became a captive of the skull lord Vargo and planned to escape.

Description
Malika's body was covered in plagues and diseases. While on Cube 1717, Malika's body was entirely covered by a magical leather outfit that included an apron, gloves, and a mask in the shape of a bird's beak with goggles made from smoked-glass. This outfit protected it from the pixelating curse and others from its inherent diseases. While it wore this outfit, it was difficult to identify Malika as a yugoloth.

Possessions
In addition to its leather outfit, Malika once owned a censer of blood, a magic item that allowed it to create vampiric mists to serve it.

Activities

While on Cube 1717, Malika was a prisoner of Vargo and was kept in its own room, guarded by two pixelated merregons. Malika wished to recover its censer of blood and escape Cube 1717.

Relationships
Vargo was unable to attach Malika's head to its own body because of the potent diseases it contained. So the skull lord hoped to get Malika to control one face of the Six-Face Throne if it could not find three more suitable heads for itself. Malika had learned almost all of Vargo's secrets.

History
The rulers of Acheron hired yugoloths to destroy Cube 1717, a part of Acheron that had become the source of the powerful pixelating curse. The yugoloths attempted to drown it in water from the Styx, but the cube escaped to the material plane and landed in the Sea of Swords on Toril. In order to finish the job, Malika was chosen to lead a group of yugoloths to finally destroy Cube 1717. They arrived on Face 5 of Cube 1717. A merrenoloth who commanded the group used ritual magic to summon water from the Styx in an attempt to isolate the Cube. Malika used its censer of blood to create seven vampiric mists and ordered them to kill anyone who tried to leave the Cube by flight. The yugoloths fought against the pixelated balhannoth controlled by Vargo and Sladek. In the fight, Malika lost its censer of blood.

However, the mission failed and most of the yugoloths were slain. Malika survived by surrendering to Vargo and three hydroloths remained in the Styx water still surrounding Cube 1717.

Appendix

Malika Tahoun's unusual clothing is based on the outfits worn by real-world plague doctors.

## Marco Creenn

Marco Creenn was an alias used by a planeswalker whose name was also misremembered as "Tuqueen" – a reluctant client of the Sharran House of Grief in the late 15 century DR.

Description
Marco was a pale and human-looking man with black disheveled head of hair. He also had a noticeably exotic accent for a Baldurian's ear.

History
In the, an unknown planeswalker appeared out of thin air, falling atop of Lenore De Hurst as she was getting ready to weave magics with her fellow Mystrans. In her later report to Lorroakan of Sorcerous Sundries, Lenore state that the magic wielded by the man was indescribable, strange, alien, not of the Weave. As he landed on Toril, the planeswalker created a planar anomaly that for a time, spirited Lenore away, trapped her between hers and some mysterious other world. From the incident, she only remembered T and Q in the man's name, possibly recalling is at "Tuqueen."

Soon after, the planeswalker took an alias of Marco Creenn and sought out the services of the House of Grief. The Mapping of the Heart revealed Elvere's "prying heart" but he disappeared before the Unburdening ritual was to take place. Marco paid for the ritual in full using alien coinage, but, as he fled, there was no refund. The strange man attracted the attention of Mother Superior of Shar, Viconia DeVir. She issued an order to track "Marco Creenn" down as during the Mapping, she detected thoughts of a strange world and stranger people, as well as thoughts fixated on a powerful artifact, a sword, or possibly a "zord," whatever it may be.

## Magic mantle

The Magic mantle was a psionic mantle that granted ardents and divine minds an array of psionics powers and abilities derived from the universal concept of magic.

Deities

Abilities
Those who followed the Magic mantle became equally in tune with the Art and the Invisible Art, treating the two as if they were but one field of power. The psionic powers of a follower of this mantle could affect magic effects, items, and spells as if they were psionic in nature. Additionally, followers became skilled in the use of magical devices.

The psychic aura exuded by divine minds of the Magic mantle made any weapons wielded by the manifester, as well as weapons wielded by any allies within the radius of the aura, be treated as though they were magic weapons for the purposes of overcoming defenses against non-magical weaponry.

Powers
Novice manifesters could grant weapons a +1 enchantment with metaphysical weapon, as well as cancel both magical and psionic effects and powers with dispel psionics. Manifesters of some experience learned how to enhance their resistance towards both powers and spells with power resistance. As a manifester progressed further they gained null psionics field, which they alone could use to create a field that functioned as both a dead-magic zone and dead-psionic zone, as well as psionic analyze dweomer, allowing them to reveal the magical history of a subject.

Followers of the Magic mantle were uniquely capable of augmenting psionic analyze dweomer, allowing the power to analyze more than just one creature or object. Masters of this mantle were granted psionic protection from spells, allowing them to make any creature more resistant to the effects of spells and spell-like abilities.

## Mass fowl

Mass fowl was a rare epic transmutation spell that allowed the caster to transform their opponents into poultry.

Effects
As of the Year of Wild Magic, 1372 DR, casting mass fowl caused every chosen target of medium or small size within 20 feet (6.1 meters) of the caster to be permanently transformed into a chicken. The casting time of the spell was short compared to normal spells.

Sufficiently powerful creatures were unaffected by this spell. Accounts varied on if the spell was subject to spell resistance. Individuals with high fortitude were sometimes able to resist the spell. It couldn't however be countered, interrupted, or dispelled using normal spells or physical attacks. To prevent the spell from being cast, one had to, for example, use an epic version of counterspell.

All items equipped by affected targets transformed into chicken were instantly destroyed upon transformation.

Development
Before it could be cast, mass fowl had to be developed. Both divine and arcane casters could develop this spell (except for warlocks). Developing an epic spell was different from learning normal spells. Once an epic spell was developed, the caster knew the spell. A developed epic spell became a part of the caster and could even be prepared without a spellbook (if a wizard was the caster). Only those well-versed in spellcraft could develop mass fowl.

Components
To cast mass fowl, the caster had to use verbal and somatic components.

Appendix
Appearances

Trivia
Neverwinter Nights 2 did not include any frog models in its original release. When epic spells were introduced in the Mask of the Betrayer expansion, many were based on content from the Epic Level Handbook. The developers may have intended to implement Mass Frog, another epic spell from that book, which functioned similarly by transforming opponents into frogs. However, for various reasons—whether budget constraints, time limitations, or simply for fun—they may have chosen to modify the spell to use an existing model of a chicken instead.

History
In, Maervidal Iloster was caught as a double agent by the Zhentarim; he received three insistent invites to a revel at Warmfires House from three different Zhentarim agents he knew within as many days, deducing they intended to kill him there because of their insistence on the invite and their insinuations they would hurt other people if he weren't to show up. Desperate and not daring leave the Dale lest he trigger a massacre that way, he crossed paths briefly with Storm Silverhand, and was struck by inspiration to ask her for help. She heard him out, then cast a spell that transformed their bodies into the shape of the other's, giving him instructions to stand in for her at the Old Skull Inn that evening while she took over for him at Warmfires.

## Marcos Flass

Marcos Flass, or Marcos the Red, was a Red Wizard of Thay and a member of the prominent Flass family, who specialized in golemcraft and creation of gemstone golems used in Thay the late 14 century DR.

Description
Marcos was a human man with a shaved head, typical for a Red Wizard. His face and scalp were decorated with tattoos.

Possessions
Marcos Flass's spellbook was bound in red and decorated with a gilded skull. He possessed a sizable collection of enchanted items, including a unique set of plates called Diamond Cut, that he offered as a reward for dealing with a band of Underdark raiders.

He wore a heavily enchanted Master's robe as well as a cape of the fire bath, bracers of armor, with a wand of fire ready to be used on his enemies.

Relationships

Marcos was a cousin of Dmitra Flass, also known as the Tharchioness and the Princess of Mulmaster.

History
Marcos was a proud member of the Flass family of Thay when, in the, he shipped a small army of gemstone golems to his cousin, Dmitra, and her husband, High Blade of Mulmaster, as an anniversary gift that was paraded across the city of Mulmaster and delivered to the Thayan embassy for the ruling couple. However, something went awry during the creation, or the constructs were used in a public assassination attempt. The constructs attacked the gathered delegates at the embassy, slaughtering half the guests, but eventually were destroyed. Marcos was blamed for the incident. The Tharchioness did not take the offense lightly and convinced Szass Tam to send her cousin away to the far end of the civilization – Icewind Dale, to Marcos's utter disdain.

Tam tasked Marcos with arranging an agreement between Termalaine's council and Thay to establish a magical research laboratory in the gem mines. During that time, still in 1373 DR, Marcos got lucky as the Ten-Towns fell victim to various disasters caused by the worshipers of godling Arctus and the man known as Iceblood summoned a supernatural blizzard that curried half the town in snow and forced the citizens to evacuate. The Red Wizard seized the opportunity, as an army of verbeegs moved into the empty town, he went on to develop a new type of construct – tourmaline golems. Little hindered Marcos's research, apart from a band of miscreants led by the duergar called Grimbold Tornhelm, who entered the mines from a passage into the Underdark in the mine's deepest reaches.

When the famed Hero of Neverwinter arrived at Termalaine, opposing Arctus, the Walking Winter, and the mysterious blue-skinned cleric, they confronted Marcos in the mines. The Hero may have had forged an agreement with the Red Wizard to help his research by ending the threat of the Underdark "guests" in exchange for the tourmaline golems' aid in the battle for Targos against the godling's hordes, which was inevitable. It was imperative for the wizard to finish his research as he hoped to pen a letter to his cousin when it was done and beg for her permission to return to Thay. However, the Hero declining to work with the wizard and ending his life was also a possible outcome of the encounter, as Marcos cared not for the fate of the Ten-Towns.

In the scroll, 'Strengthening of the Sword Arm' was the teaching that dictated the Sharrans were to work on melee combat drills for two hours daily, changing the weapon and the opponent after each consecutive round. During such exercises, wounds were permitted, and the church members prided themselves on the scars they earned. 'Honing of the Archer's Eye' was the second drill; it took two hours per day, teaching Sharrans to shoot at still, moving, and later even live targets. 'Hardening of the Poisoner's Heart' covered the theory of poison-making and was taught for another two hours per day. Each of the cloister students was dosed with small amounts of various poisons to develop tolerance.

In the, a copy of Martial Catechism was found within the Cloister of Sombre Embrace, a secret Sharran sect underneath the Lower City of Baldur's Gate and available from the House of Grief above it.

## Malar's tomb

Malar's tomb, alternatively called the Beastlord's tomb and sometimes referred to as Malar's temple, was a holy site dedicated to the god Malar located on the island of Moray in the Moonshae Isles.

Location
The tomb lay in a cave beneath Scourtop, the northernmost peak of the Orcskull Mountains in the south of Moray. It was only accessible via a ruined city in a vale beneath the mountain's summit.

Structure
A huge square opening in the granite mountainside served as the entryway. This was effectively a massive, cube-shaped porch lined with marble. In the back of this porch was a much older cave dug into the mountainside, which was blackened with soot and lined with torches set in iron fittings.

Interior
At the end of this tunnel, deep inside the heart of Scourtop, was a rough-hewn chamber of reddish rock with a blood-stained floor of agate tiles. This chamber was ringed by thirteen basalt columns fitted with iron chains and manacles for stringing up sacrifices, and at the center of the room was a human-height table of light stone covered in glyphs and with lanterns on two ends. Air vents leading to the surface provided enough oxygen for the fires.

Activities
Rituals in the tomb were held each new moon, and involved thirteen adherents of Malar and copious blood sacrifices.

History
Believed to have originally been a primitive shrine dedicated to one or more Primordials, it was consecrated as a temple to Malar following its discovery by members of the Black Blood tribe.

During the period when Malar was "dead" following the Spellplague, his steaming corpse lay in this tomb upon the table as a centerpiece for sacrifices and rituals attempting to revive him, which were led by his angelic servant, Argon Bael. A prophecy held that the revival of Malar required both a cleric of a consenting greater deity and a special sacrifice to serve as his vessel. In the late 1470s DR, both of these criteria were met when Argon Bael was made aware by High Lady Ordalf of Sarifal that two individuals were headed to the island: a priestess of Chauntea named Marikke and an empathic cat-shifter named Kip. Bael and his allies in the Black Blood tribe captured these two, brought them to the tomb, and with torture and coercion, successfully managed to revive Malar within the body of Kip (although the ritual also cost Bael his life).

Following Malar's resurrection, his former tomb then served as his temple as he gained strength before calling for a High Hunt and inciting the Battle of Caer Moray. As of, sacrifices continued to be offered in the shrine each dark of the moon.

In 1479 DR, a young Northlander noble named Daffyd Mac Lyrr discovered a map that he believed pointed to the Black Blood's temple of Malar, and he concocted a plan to attack it and decapitate the tribe. However, the map he discovered pointed to a defunct temple that had instead become the lair of the purple dragon known as Whitescar.

Inhabitants
Black Blood lycanthropes loyal to Malar served him within the tomb, although only predatory lycanthropes (such as werewolves) were allowed within its depths.

## Madness

Madness or insanity was a broad term describing a variety of mental illnesses, conditions, symptoms, and disorders that could affect people in subtle or dramatic ways. In the Realms, they were commonly called afflictions of the mind.

Causes

Terrible shocks were a reliable source of sanity loss, especially for those that pursued dramatic and perilous events like adventurers. These could be events of "mundane" grief and horror—having a friend die, coming across a gory scene, or being tortured—or distinctly supernatural—seeing someone turn to stone from a medusa's gaze, witnessing an alien planar being or even a god in the flesh. The skills and worldview of someone informed what affected them to an extent—a martial warrior would likely be inured to physical violence but broken by supernatural threats, while mages could more easily intellectualize the supernatural but be revolted by mundane carnage. Priests were usually inured to mundane and magical perils, but were particularly sensitive to spiritual affronts and blasphemous deeds that threatened their divinely-ordered worldview. Roguish sorts could more easily protect their mental health with a perceived distance born of cunning, secrecy, and aloofness—until the moment their stratagems collapsed and it all became distinctly personal.

Those who made direct telepathic contact with other beings were at risk of being damaged by the experience if they were sufficiently strange or shocking. It was dangerous for humans to come into contact with the minds of aberrations like beholders, morkoths, and cloakers, and it was a struggle to interface with  like treants and phycomids. Planar beings like elementals (including golems) and fiends were also dangerously alien, including when facilitated by contact other plane. It was also hazardous for initial expectations to be harshly subverted—such as discovering that the telepathic target was actually a disguised doppelganger—or making contact with those already under mind-influencing effects like charming or dominating magic. Most insidiously, it was risky for a telepath to come into contact with those suffering mental illness, as it could spread from person to person, even in the course of healing them.

Other, more obscure forms of sanity erosion could be found in the world, such as:
 Even a sliver of divine omniscience could drive a limited mortal mind mad.
 Eating illithid brains caused madness in the consumer.
 The plane of Pandemonium innately assailed inhabitants with mental strain, likely driving them to some form of madness, minor or major. Signs of this mental instability were regarded as a good trait for companions in the Outer Planes, as it indicated they had visited Pandemonium and returned mostly intact.
 The Spellplague caused physical and mental changes in those it touched, often for the worse. The plaguechanged were usually violently mad, and creeping madness caused further mental damage.
 Hill giants that were starved into insanity became known as mouths of Grolantor, driven by an incurable hunger and anxiety.

Magic

Arcanists that specialized in strange and alien magics were much more likely to stress their minds with alien knowledge, which eroded their sanity and ability to live in the mundane world. These included necromancers, alienists, fleshwarpers, aberrant minds, and anyone else who dealt with horrors best left beyond comprehension.

Some spells created extraordinary anxiety and fear in the target, causing them to be wracked with panic. While these were relatively gentle compared to other mental attacks, they still left lasting mental wounds that could worsen over time. This included spells like fear, doom, cause fear, scare, and symbol of fear. Terrifying illusions, if believed in, were also perfectly capable of shocking the victim and damaging their mental state as if they had seen the real thing.

Many spells (mainly enchantment magics) directly influenced the mental state of the target, and in some cases caused thoughts and behaviour described as mad or insane; many of these could be found as part of the Madness domain:
 Bolts of devilment left the target reeling in confusion, unable to act or even form coherent thoughts.
 Confusion caused a generalized disordering of thoughts, random behavior, and potentially self-destructive decision-making. Spells that caused similar effects included chaos, sphere of chaos, insanity, rigid thinking, symbol of insanity, and jester song.
 Cloak of insanity caused a kind of surface-level insanity in the target, which then protected them from mental attacks and psychic intrusions.
 Chaos field left a powerful mark on reality, including driving living creatures mad.
 Maddening scream left the target screaming incomprehensibly as their mind broke.
 Righteous wrath of the faithful, which filled allies with a fierce battle madness directed at enemies.
 Touch of madness, which left the victim dazed and confused as their mind clouded over.

Magical Items

Many magical items could be used to cause general mental unwellness similar to confusion, temporarily or permanently. This included the harp of Pandemonium, harp of discord, scarab of insanity, and Joril's dagger.

Cursed magical items sometimes imparted some sort of self-destructive behavior in the bearer:
 Berserker axe, which made the bearer murderously insane.
 Elixir of madness, a potion that did as described.
 Insanity's Kiss, a potion that caused a murderous rage in the imbiber.
 The Faces of Madness, Imaskari relics that carried terrible curses, mental and physical.

Duration
Acquired mental illness could be fitted to three broad categories, depending on their severity, duration, and how they could be addressed:

 Short-term "temporary insanity" usually lasted from minutes to days as the mind reeled from some immense shock, psychic assault, or revelation, and displayed obvious behavioural changes in that time. After they gathered their wits and recovered, there was still usually signs of the experience remaining as strange quirks and mannerisms.
 Long-term "indefinite insanity" was the typical persistent form of mental unwellness, often lasting for months or years at minimum. It required dedicated treatment in the form of friendly company, medication, therapy, and good rest. Even after the most serious symptoms and triggers were addressed, the patient was still marked by the experience for the rest of their life.
 "Permanent insanity" was the most severe form, and was generally incurable even with the assistance of powerful magics. The individual suffered an irrevocable and massive shift in their ability to address reality and the nature of their own thoughts, never to be restored. They might be left unable to function and survive, or be left almost entirely undisturbed until the moment it was triggered without warning.

Treatment

In the Realms, it was understood that the best treatment for mental illness was found at home. Those in distress were first tended to by local priests and respected elders like family matriarchs, who kept company with the afflicted and let them speak of what troubled them while sipping on calming herbal teas and cordials. Priests and temples then took the lead on therapeutic, medicinal, and magical healing for mental afflictions and assisting the friends and family throughout the process. This level of care earned priesthoods the genuine and wide-reaching appreciation of folk on Toril, adding to the temporal power of the churches.

Clerics provided the bulk of magical treatment and healing. This included inducing peacing sleep, invoking dreams to open the mind, and various other mental enchantments to soothe and rest. Specific spells included:
 General-purpose healing spells such as restoration and heal could cure or mediate most illnesses, with limited wish and wish able to address more powerful afflictions.
 Atonement helped resolve the trauma of evil actions.
 Calm emotions and pacification could temporarily suppress some mental afflictions and magical influences.
 Feeblemind could be used as a kind of treatment for extreme mental illness, as it caused the stoppage of all thoughts and granted the target relief from mental anguish.
 Psychic chirurgery could be used to cure all manner of mental conditions.
 Remove fear could be used to reduce the magnitude of recent fear-based trauma.

Medicines were a vital part of not just physical but also mental healthcare in the Realms. Alchemists, local wise women, and traveling priests provided remedies that helped address symptoms and further other treatments.
 Tea made from feverbalm could temporarily suppress some mental afflictions.
 Noblestalk was a mushroom that helped to heal certain neurological illnesses.

Types of Madness

Afflictions of the mind took many forms, and was rarely simple and clear to understand. Delusions presented false aspects of reality and the self; anxieties, obsessions, and compulsions dominated thoughts and behaviours; mood could be driven by depression and mania; and dissociation blocked out parts of memory and personality. Some specific afflictions of the mind included:

 Addiction, a chronic dependency on a substance or activity.
 Amnesia, the loss of some or all memories.
 Catatonia, a complete withdrawal of the mind from reality.
 Delusional insanity, a persistent and grandly incorrect understanding of themselves and reality.
 Demarcation, a specific inability to separate delusion from reality, tied to psionics and the Underdark.
 Dementia, a general loss of cognitive function, often with age.
 False memories, the presence of modified or implanted memories.
 Hallucinations, the perception of things that weren't real.
 Homicidal mania, an uncontrollable desire to destroy and kill.
 Kleptomania, a powerful and arbitrary urge to steal.
 Lost one, a person shattered by the Domains of Dread.
 Megalomania, a massively exaggerated self-perception of ability and importance.
 Melancholy, a crushing loss of happiness and willpower.
 Multiple personalities, the presence of more than one persona or mind in the same body.
 Paranoia, an overwhelming suspicion and distrust of others.
 Phobias, intense fears or aversions to certain concepts.
 Pyromania, an unhealthy fondness for fire.

Places of Treatment
Institutions that gave treatment were available for the care of the unwell, such as temples, asylums, and hospitals. Though this (usually) meant a certain level of professional care, it also meant a disconnection from home and familiar faces, and a dependence on strangers in a strange place. Some places even mistreated their patients, whether from negligence or malice.
 The Cloister of St. Ramedar was an Ilmatari temple that specialized in treating the mentally ill.
 The House of the Golden Quill in Waterdeep provided care for those mentally damaged by magic.
 The Sanatorium of Helm's Hold became an asylum for those with spellscars and corresponding mental instability.
 Thornthar was a lodge for housing and caring for retired servants of Cormyr, especially those with senility.
 Spellhold was ostensibly a place of safety and treatment for those with mental instability and magical power, but was really more of a prison and laboratory used by the Cowled Wizards.
 Zellix the mind flayer operated an asylum in order to lure in and detain the mad, who Zellix believed had the tastiest brains.

Sufferers of Madness
Notable Individuals with Madness
 Aribeth de Tylmarande suffered great melancholy after the execution of Fenthick Moss, and was driven to vengeful and self-destructive despair through visions sent by Morag.
 Fernd Krip was depressed after a heartbreak, and was then manipulated and driven to madness by Loru, a death slaad in disguise.
 Halaster Blackcloak was an extraordinary and powerfully insane archmage who insinuated himself in Undermountain.
 Rohini the succubus was exposed to the Hex Locus by the Abolethic Sovereignty, becoming lost in prophetic visions and adopting a new mindset of sorts.
 Sarith Kzekarit was slowly driven insane while fungal spores grew in his brain.
 Soman Galt, Mayor of Neverwinter, became increasingly eccentric and mentally damaged while suffering under the mental domination of the Abolethic Sovereignty, without being consciously aware of their existence.
 Wanev, Director of Spellhold, was quite sane until Jon Irenicus experimented on him and broke his mind. He then became a patient at his own asylum.

Creatures with Madness
Some kinds of creatures were particularly likely to have mental instability, or had patterns of thought that resembled it:
 Beholders had a unique kind of insanity endemic to their kind comprised largely of chronic xenophobia and paranoia. The rare few sane beholders were outcasts among their kin, and regarded as dangerous threats.
 Derro were prone to eccentricities and quirks, in some cases turning into full madness.
 Duergar had a kind of shared psychic trauma from ancestral mind flayer torments, exacerbated by alcohol.
 Kuo-toa were chronically insane after surviving the influence of mind flayers.
 Medusae were turned into monsters by their pride, vanity, and lust for power. This transformation could drive them mad, and having to subsequently live with their condition usually broke them.
 Nothics were arcanists physically and mentally broken by the pursuit of dark and dangerous lore.

Powers with Madness

While it was normal for beings of power to have eccentricities and inscrutable goals, some had such strong obsessions, compulsions, and disordered thoughts that they could only be described as mad. Many of these gods also embodied the Madness domain, and their instability was passed on to their divine servants, followers, and magical boons. The spells that they granted to their priests often warped the perception of reality or thought processes, such as bolts of bedevilment, confusion, insanity, maddening scream, phantasmal killer, rage, touch of madness, and weird. Such gods included:
 Blibdoolpoolp, who was the patron of the kuo-toa and their madness.
 Cyric, self-declared patron of strife, madness, and lies, who grew madder by the day.
 Diinkarazan was trapped in the prison of Ilsensine and driven terribly mad by the torments.
 Ghaunadaur, who lurked alone in the Dismal Caverns and fermented in madness.
 The Great Mother was considered insane, but may have simply been too alien to be comprehended by lesser minds.
 Lolth's sanity broke after being banished to the Abyss, making her desires contradictory and self-defeating at times, and she imparted this self-destructive mindset upon her drow followers.
 Tharizdun spread madness and destruction through its followers.
 Vecna shared dark and terrible secrets with his followers.

Appendix
Behind the Scenes
While various forms of mental illness have been used from the start in the Dungeon Masters Guide 1st edition, their appearance and use is defined more by dramatic conventions in ancient and modern storytelling than precise medical understanding. Ed Friedlander advised that given the widespread prevalence and harsh impact of mental illness in real life, tabletop insanity should ideally take an unrealistic form—heroically grand (and entertaining) fixations, compulsions, fears, and delusions that drive rather than hinder gameplay and the enjoyment thereof.

## Marabaldia

Princess Marabaldia was the daughter of a powerful fomorian royal family of the Underdark beneath the island of Gwynneth in the Moonshae Isles as of the late 15 century DR.

Description
She was said to be the most beautiful fomorian maiden of her time, although this meant little to anyone who was not a fomorian as she was still a giant with purple, wart-covered skin and a distinctive fomorian "evil eye" which was budging and glowed yellow. However, such was the strength of her character that even those who saw her as ugly would occasionally glimpse a fleeting sense of how fomorians saw her.

Personality

Marabaldia was merciful, modest, and discreet, and she conducted herself with tact and polite formality. She was gentle and fiercely loyal to her friends, and feared that her non-fomorian friends might think that they only liked her because of the magic of her eye. She could be awkward and distant around those she loved.

Abilities
Her "evil eye" allowed her to alter the perceptions and slow the thoughts of those she gazed upon, although she protested against characterizing it as a "weapon". Those who saw their reflections in her eye were also prone to self-reflection.

Relationships
She regarded the gnome Suka as a close and important friend, although one whom she was prone to treat more like a child than an equal. Following the trials they endured together, she had become very fond of a song that Suka would sing, an overly melancholy tune called Oh, Father Dear. As fomorian royalty, Marabaldia had long benefitted from the enslavement of other races, especially gnomes, but she did not seem to question this or to recognize how this made Suka uncomfortable.

She bore a great anger at the leShay rulers of Sarifal: at Prince Araithe for betraying her and at the High Lady Ordalf for imprisoning her for a decade.

She deeply loved her childhood sweetheart, Ughoth, who was a prince of a rival tribe. They shared a juvenile love: the pair were awkward together and never consummated their relationship before his untimely death.

History
Marabaldia was the daughter of one of nine powerful royal families who ruled the fomorian tribes in the Underdark beneath the Winterglen forest on Gwynneth, but her father abandoned her when she was very young, leaving her to be raised by her mother. Growing up, she was renown for her beauty and her musical and artistic talents. She would eventually fall in love with Ughoth, a young fomorian from a different tribe. While her mother acquiesced to their desire to wed, and a date was set for the wedding, it was at that time that her father reentered her life to insist that she marry a different bridegroom, one who was rich but old and ugly. Marabaldia and Ughoth fled, and after may close calls, managed to escape to the surface. They emerged in the cellars beneath Citadel Umbra, where they were welcomed by the leShay prince of Sarifal, Araithe. However, he soon betrayed them, imprisoning Marabaldia and selling Ughoth to the fomorians pursuing them. She was subsequently sent south to a hidden prison beneath Caer Corwell. Unbeknownst to her, the leShay used her as a hostage to extract concessions from the fomorians relating to the Pact of Eschatos.

Marabaldia was kept in a dark, cramped cell of iron bars that was specially designed such that some bars could be removed to adjoin her cell to another cage. High Lady Ordalf, in her cruelty, would place her enemies in this cage and slowly starve Marabaldia over a tenday as the bars were gradually removed in an attempt to force her to kill and eat her fellow prisoners. She kept track of the passing years with tick marks on her wall.

After ten years in this jail, having never even been given a change of clothes, she escaped in the late 1470s DR with the help of fellow prisoners, the lycanthrope Poke and the gnome Suka. Symbolically, Marabaldia claimed one of the iron bars from her cell as a weapon. During their escape, they were accosted by Prince Ariathe himself, who made grand and empty overtures of apology to Marabaldia, claiming that her imprisonment had been a misunderstanding and a mistake. Meanwhile, he attempted to use his magic to compel Suka to kill Marabaldia with a crossbow and have an enslaved cyclops named Borgol kill Suka, thus allowing him to focus on capturing his true target, Poke, to interrogate her about the whereabouts of her mistress, Amaranth. However, Marabaldia saw through this scheme and used the power of her evil eye to help Suka break Ariathe's control. The trio brought down Araithe, but despite having him at her mercy, Marabaldia insisted that they spare him (despite Suka's protests). They fled from the ruins of Caer Corwell, but were set upon by Araithe's drow mercenaries. They were only saved by the intervention of Captain Rurik of the Winterglen Claw and Lord Mindarion of Synnoria, who recognized Marabaldia and greeted her as a princess. Unfortunately, both Poke and Borgol lost their lives to the drow as the group fled Caer Corwell.

The group journeyed to Harrowfast in the Cambro Mountains above Synnoria where a burgeoning alliance was being negotiated between the humans of the Winterglen Claw, the Llewyrr elves of the Knights of Synnoria, and the fomorians of the nine tribes. To her shock, she discovered that her father was dead and the armies of the nine tribes had been united and were now led by her former lover, Ughoth, with whom she tentatively renewed her courtship. As she was still recognized as a fomorian princess, Marabaldia participated in the negotiations, although she was largely ignored by the haughty Llewyrr. The alliance soon broke down following a violent outbreak between some of the elves against Rurik and Suka, which then led to violence between the fomorians and elves as Marabaldia chose to protect her friend. Despite recognizing that Suka was perhaps at fault in the altercation, Marabaldia showed no outward blame against her small friend, even after Ughoth succumbed to wounds he received in the fighting.

Marabaldia and her fomorian followers fled north through the Underdark, where they encountered two of Suka's allies, Lukas and Gaspar-shen, as well as Lady Amaranth, all of whom were being pursued by the army of Prince Araithe. Despite Marabaldia's grim willingness to battle the prince again, Amaranth parlayed with him to allow the rest to escape. Suka would then leave Gwynneth with Lukas and Gaspar-shen.

## Mage wine

Mage wine was a fusion of potion and wine that granted certain arcane spellcasters who imbibed it the power to immediately recall a spell they had cast earlier in the day.

Powers
The effects of mage wine would only trigger when the drink was imbibed by a bard or wizard.

History
Sometime in the late 14 century DR, in the month of Uktar or "The Rotting", a cult dedicated to the dead power Moander and backed by the deity Ghaunadaur chose The Hallow-Halls in Ravens Bluff to be the second site in their series of attacks with an experimental gas weapon that had been made near Dark Hollow. They narrowed it down to the shrine of the Seldarine, as they were rivals of Ghaunadaur. A Moanderite in green robes tried to enter the shrine, but was stopped at the door by temple guards. He chose to drop the vial there, unleashing the gas weapon and killing dozens of innocent Ravenians, as well as a nearby unit of City Watchmen that had rushed over to aid the temple guards. All exposed to the green gas were disintegrated, leaving behind no bodies. A group of adventurers working for the Scout Rangers arrived on the scene shortly after, having been alerted to the attack by the sounds of screaming and a panicking crowd.

After the adventurers brought those responsible to justice, the priests at the Seldarine shrine sent them two potions of extra-healing and two bottles of mage wine as a show of thanks for the aid they provided.

## Magelords of Athalantar

The Magelords of Athalantar were a cabal of mages risen to rulership of the kingdom of Athalantar in the early-to-mid 3 century DR.

Organization
Constituted under the authority of Belaur Aumar, the Magelords mostly answered to Ithboltar among their number.

Three among their number also took the title of Mage Royal: Ubriien Orlyn until his death on Eleint 11 of the, then Neldryn Hawklyn until his death in the, and finally Undarl until the .

Abilities

Activities
The Magelords ruled Athalantar by any measure, with their upper echelon being largely left to their own devices, be it teaching, spell research, or hunting. Their apprentices, also magelords in name, acted as their enforcers.

Base of Operations
Though many of the Magelords traveled the realm doing the bidding of their leadership, the ones highest among their ranks were known to spend most of their time around Athalgard proper.

History
Originally, the Magelords were a number of wizards trained by Ithboltar, their eldest, who came at the request of a favored pupil, Neldryn Hawklyn. Initially friends of Prince Belaur Aumar, they took over ruling functions for him after he hired them to seize the throne of Athalantar, a task they completed in the . Afterwards, among other activities, the Magelords attacked the Wyrmtower of Shandrath, slaying him in a massed attack in the, transformed Prince Nrymm Aumar into an otyugh, battled Felodar Aumar's own hired mages, and inducted the stranger mage Undarl into their ranks after he slew Prince Elthryn Aumar in the .

The organization was forcefully disbanded in  after the death of King Belaur, as well as just about the entirety of their leadership.

Members
Originally a band of mages from a faraway land, the Magelords eventually came to bolster their numbers by pressing into service every magician passing through Athalantar who didn't do so undetected. A number of them joined in other circumstances, either originally as their foes, or by petitioninh entry, such as Undarl. The total number of magelords, in that way, varied between thirty and forty at all times between  and .

## Marikke

Marikke was a Ffolk priestess of Chauntea from Alaron in the Moonshae Isles prior to her death in the late 15 century DR.

Description
Her hair was long, stiff, and yellow, and would hang down over her face as she prayed.

Personality
She was devoted to her goddess, and took comfort in her presence. She gladly recited long litanies of prayers—the nineteen formal prayers and twenty-one codicils—despite how time-consuming and exhausting this could be. She was interested in the ways that the gods interacted or related to each other, and had privately entertained the thought that all gods might just be extensions of one singular divinity.

She liked to have her own personal space.

Abilities
Marikke's Chauntea-given powers allowed her to heal others, to heighten her allies' skills, and to grant speed and good fortune on the high seas.

Relationships
She assumed the role of adoptive mother to Kip, an orphaned cat-shifter from Alaron. She loved him very deeply, and the thought of losing him brought her great grief.

Marikke was one of the newest members of the crew of the Sphinx, and helped to tend the sails and pray for good winds. She was indebted to the ship's captain, Lukas, for helping her out of a desperate situation. She distrusted the Savage, in part because she distrusted all elves (whom she saw as arrogant), and she was in turn distrusted by Suka.

History
Marikke was born in an upland village on Alaron. She trained as a priestess of Chaunte, and became well-versed in the stories of various gods. At some point, she adopted the starving Kip and provided him with a home at her father's house.

One spring in the late 1470s DR, Marikke left Kip at an inn she could not afford as she desperately sought work and a guildhall in Caer Callidyrr. This was when she met Lukas, who recruited her as a healer for an upcoming job after he learned of her and Kip's plight.

The job in question was to escort Lord Aldon Kendrick to the ruins of Caer Corwell in Sarifal, but the Sphinx was greeted there by High Lady Ordalf, the ruler of Sarifal, who killed Aldon and tasked the crew with killing her half-sister, Lady Amaranth, who led a group of lycanthropes on the island of Moray. During these interactions, the High Lady Ordalf expressed her disdain for Kip and mocked Marikke for being a woman aboard a ship of mostly males. Unbeknownst to the crew, Ordalf had determined during their meeting that Marikke and Kip were the keys to fulfilling a prophecy for the return of Malar, a "dead" god worshiped by the Black Blood tribe on Moray. Thinking that she would not mind if Malar were to arise and kill Amaranth instead of the crew of the Sphinx, Ordalf contacted Argon Bael, a Malarite angel of vengeance, and coordinated signals to let him know that they were coming to Moray. When the Sphinx was sunk by fire nagas, Marikke, Kip, and the Savage were ambushed and captured by Argon Bael and his followers upon reaching Moray's shore.

The hostages were taken to the city below Scourtop and into Malar's tomb, where Argon Bael revealed that both Marikke and Kip were needed for the success of the ritual to revive his god. He told Marikke that her goddess's affirmation was required to raise Malar from death, and while Marikke could not believe this, it was confirmed by Chauntea herself in a vision granted to Marikke as she was subjected to torture meant to compel Kip to give himself as the vessel for Malar's return. Already confused and afraid that her goddess would desire the return of an evil god at the expense of her and Kip, Marikke became despondent when the Savage attempted to intervene and stop the ritual, and was revealed to be a hated daemonfey. When the dust settled, Argon Bael was dead, the Savage had been captured again, and Kip had become an aspect of Malar. Afraid of both her goddess and of the Savage, Marikke clung to the hope that Kip's personality would resurface, and became a servant of Malar.

Only a couple days later, she finally confronted the Savage, whom "Kip" had ordered her to kill, and while she found him to be irredeemable, she was stung by his accusations of betrayal and decided to help him escape. She confronted "Kip" and tried to remind him of his old self, but Malar lost patience with her. His werewolves dismembered her body and burned its pieces on his altar. Chauntea did not approve of this treatment of her priestess, and turned against Malar when he tried to conquer Moray the following day.

## Maos

Maos was a mysterious island that arose from the Moonsea every Shieldmeet when the sun set and sank at dawn's light.

History
There were no written historical records of the island, but sages theorized it must have been part of an ancient human kingdom some time before . Moreover, no evidence was found for why Maos sank and rose, with the most likely explanation being magic, such as a curse invoked by ancient priests or even direct divine intervention.

Geography
Found roughly  south from Phlan,This is in contradiction to the map provided in the same sourcebook boxed set, The Moonsea, which shows Maos as "Moas" and north of Hillsfar. Given Moas is not further mentioned in the sourcebooks, this is assumed to be in error and the name will be kept as written. the island was perfectly circlular at precisely  in diameter. Its sudden rise to the surface during Shieldmeet generated great churning waves and sea foam. At dawn's light, the island quickly sank, creating a whirlpool that could drag ships within  of it below the waves.

Description
All around the island could be found dying fish, aquatic plant life and wet slime from its time at the seabed.

Below the surface, a labyrinthine network of caverns could be found.

On its surface were a number of structures. The grandest was a spire standing  high and built from a black and green stone that glistened with the moisture. This was widely believed to be a temple, but to an unknown deity. Underneath the altar could be found passage to the caverns below the island.

Another structure was a roofless observatory, circular in design, as well as all black in color. Strange symbols were inscribed all over the interior, while small stones jutted from the floor.

Several less remarkable structures were two or three stories tall, one of which also provided access to the caverns below. These structures were bare and empty.

Powers
The most dangerous feature of the island was its ability to negate all clerical magic (even magic items imbued with clerical magic).

Inhabitants
The island had no permanent population, but creatures that had been known to lair in the buildings were lacedons, kuo-toa, merrow, and scrags. Sea fauna such as giant octopi, giant crabs, and lampreys had also been seen.

Legends

The bard Mendryll Belarod, in his travels across the Moonsea, learned a little regarding the mysterious island. The existence of Maos was mostly known to sailors and sages, but the greater details of the island remained a mystery to both. Some sages claimed that Maos was a city of learning, or that it was even the home of an ancient human kingdom, predating the elves.

Mariners claimed the island was guarded by sea-creatures, even the animated dead of past victims. A great curse was said to be on the island, known only as "The Curse of Godly Silence."Possibly in reference to the island's ability to negate clerical magic. More positive rumors spoke of deep treasure vaults, full of long-forgotten spells, ancient artifacts and sentient swords.

## Maerend Skeldragon

Maerend Skeldragon was a half-elf adventurer and chef who traveled across the lands of southeast Faerûn in the 15 century DR.

Description
Maerend had blond hair, a very slender frame, and an agile, attractive body.

Personality
His personality could be described as mischievous.

Activities
He occasionally worked as a caravan guard, protecting valuable cargo. Over time he was part of two separate adventuring companies, the defunct Valade's Shields of Morvar and Telmark's Stalwarts in Suldolphor, the latter of which fluctuated in its activity.

History
Over the course of his life as an explorer, Maerend visited many of the nations of southeast Faerûn, including Durpar, Estagund, Luiren, Thommar, Ulgarth, and Var the Golden. Beyond southeast Faerûn he had explored the Tashalar, a little of the nation of Chondath, and the highlands and ranges of the Yehimal Mountains east of Ulgarth. As he journeyed across these varied lands, Maerend cooked dishes using the local herbs, flowers, and wildlife. Of all the dishes he ever concocted, his favorite evenfeast was a roasted hraztam in Ulgarth. For this he stuffed it with roasted chestnuts, dulthunn (a local variety of spinach), shallots, and his own combination of seasonings.
