## Mantari

Mantari were flying creatures that closely resembled manta rays except for the fact that they flew in the air instead of swimming in the seas.

Description
Like manta rays they had flat wide bodies, although they were quite smaller than their marine counterparts only being   long and  wide. Also unlike manta rays, they had  long tails with stingers on their ends.

Combat

When mantari engaged prey, they would do so by pointing their tail-stinger down and targeting their prey's nervous system. Diving down from, they would attempt to ambush their prey. By attacking the nervous system they were able to near-paralyze unfortunate victims, and once a target lay immobilized the mantaris would begin to feed.

Ecology
They usually preyed on giant rats and their like, but would, when driven by hunger, target humans and demihumans alike.
They lived in packs and would hunt together, bringing their numbers to bear on larger and more dangerous prey.

Twice a year, they had a mating season whereupon the males would compete in aerial maneuvers to impress the females. They bore two to five young who were born live while the females were in flight, and the parents would be quite protective of their young for the first two months of their lives.

Habitat
The mantari were often found in dirty dungeon caverns where their prey abounded. They especially liked to lay still on the cavern floor and hiding until prey were close by, and might be mistaken for puddles of dirty water.

Training
A mantari young, if captured within a week of its birth, could be reliably trained and become a loyal pet, guarding and protecting its master, while keeping vermin infestations down. Such trained mantaris often went for as much as 200 gp on the open market.

Notable Mantari
 Vleem, the companion and friend of Emrock Uerngulphim.

Rumors
Sages were constantly debating whether they were kin to manta rays or related to cloakers, trappers, or lurkers.

## Marcus Rubicon

Marcus Rubicon was the field general of Ravens Bluff in the Vast during the mid–14 century DR.

Description
At the time of his retirement, he was a middle-aged man with steel-gray hair and brown eyes.

Personality
The man was responsible, and openly mindful of his reputation.

Possessions
He bore a Marshal's Rod, and his office was covered in enemy standards, presumably from vanquished forces.

Relationships
He was served by two staffers, Malcom and Duncan. The rod he bore marked him as a member of the Knights of the Raven who'd presided over forces in a victorious battle.

History
Marcus Rubicon had once been feted in a festival for a victory over Zhentarim forces. His office was rich in enemy standards that had presumably been taken from defeated enemies.

Years later, before being replaced by Charles Frederik LaVerne Blacktree IV as field general of Ravens Bluff, an event that took place in the, Marcus Rubicon had been responsible for dispatching a patrol to Stag Falls, a nearby town under the protection of Ravens Bluff, after noticing they'd missed the annual taxes. Noticing the patrol had not returned for two weeks, he had adventurers briefed and sent there to investigate.The undated 1995 Polyhedron article states he has been replaced by Blacktree already. However, the 1998 adventure has him not yet replaced; Charles becomes Field General after demonstrating himself in combat by, through the War of Ravens Bluff. With Rubicon not mentioned through those events in any way, the timeline is suspect, and this date may be replaced as more information becomes available.

## Maiden of Highpeak

The maiden of Highpeak, also called the maid of Highpeak, was a mysterious and legendary woman whose anguished cries could be heard echoing across southern Moray in the Moonshae Isles as of the mid–14 century DR.

History
Her cries were heard and documented by Elminster during his visit to the Moonshaes in the early-to-mid 14 century DR. He transcribed her tale as told by King Dagdar of Moray, and speculated that the king himself might have been a descendant of the maiden.

Rumors & Legends

According to an old Moonshae tale, the maiden and her many sons dwelt in peace and isolation within a grand castle of glass high in the Orcskull Mountains. The sons grew tired of living in the castle, and so they constructed a glass bridge to a nearby mountain, and set out to explore. However, as they left, the castle disappeared. The sons would go on to become mercenaries, and all but the eldest would end up dying in battle. After many years, this lone and much older survivor returned home and rediscovered the bridge during a bitter winter. As he crossed it, he slipped on the ice and fell to his death. The maiden was grief-stricken, and her cries could henceforth be heard echoing out of the mountains during hot summers or freezing winters. The tale concluded with the thought that, one day, a descendant of the maiden would rediscover the castle and relieve the mother's suffering.

## Mamlukkar

Mamlukkar, the Slave's Village was a town inside Shoonach, capital complex of the Shoon Imperium.

Geography
Mamlukkar was in western Shoonach, attached to the Imperial City and surrounded by the Fedhiyajar lands. It was a relatively short distance from the port of Agis on the River Agis.

Description
In its time the town was devoted to housing and containing the slave population of Shoonach. Even after thousands of years, ancient dwarven water pumps from High Shanatar continued to pump fresh water to the surface which was then used in fountains. It was walled in with its initial construction, and following the destruction of the city the walls were expanded and extended again to 15 feet high in order to contain the danger within.

History
Mamlukkar was built after  when the construction efforts of Shoonach began. It was created alongside the Imperial City, serving as the home for Shoonach's slaves.

In 450 DR Prince Strohm I slew Emperor Amahl Shoon VII and destroyed the city in the Great Fires of Shoonach. Mamlukkar was abandoned, only receiving expanded walls in order to contain a deadly plague that emerged in the slave village, then was carried by its undead victims.

Inhabitants
By the mid-14 century DR, Mamlukkar was still home to large amounts of moaning and rotting undead, carrying a plague that the walls had contained for centuries. It was also home to peculiar remnant's of Shoon's slave-containment measures, such as living walls. The ruins were also inhabited by orc zombies and skeletons from the Black Horde.

## Maridlands

The Maridlands were a short-lived realm belonging to the marid Ajhuu and his followers, former vassals of the great genie Calim.

Description
Though also an imperial conqueror like Calim, Ajhuu was noticably less tyrannical towards his subjects, and allowed them greater freedoms than in the Calim Empire.

Geography
The Maridlands split from the Calim Empire, taking the lands west of the Alimir Mountains centered on the newly-built coastal city of Ajhuutal.

History
When Calim paused his expansionism in  in order to avoid the ire of the local Shanatar dwarves and the elves of Tethir and Darthiir, some of his vassals took this as a sign of weakness. When he turned his efforts to exterminating the giants and dragons of the Marching Mountains, the marid Ajhuu seized the eastern extents of the Calim Empire for himself, forming the Maridlands. By the time Calim noticed the treachery and reoriented his forces in, Ajhuu was well-established and fought to maintain his independence, leading to the Steam Clashes. Unable to bear the appearance of fallibility any longer (an unacceptable state for a tyrannical overlord), in  Calim caused the Shattering, which obliterated Ajhuu, his capital, the Maridlands, and a good chunk of the Calim Empire with it.

## Mage Purges

The Mage Purges was a bloody and destructive campaign of wizard-killing perpetuated by Emperor Amahl Shoon VII between 427 DR and his death in 450 DR.

History
Emperor Amahl inaugurated his reign in 427 DR by expressing his rampant paranoia and hatred of those who could use arcane magic, starting wide-ranging purges and killings of suspected arcanists, their families, and their allies. The worst of the purges occurred in the first year of his reign, with more than 38,000 people slain and 44,000 fled to other lands due to presumed connections to the arcane arts, and every mage academy and guildhouse razed. Perpetuated by Shoon soldiers and common mobs driven to a frenzy, the Purges lost intensity after the first year but remained in effect until the destruction of the Shoon Imperium in 450 DR.

It was speculated that these purges and the mass exodus led to upheavals in other lands as the mages resettled themselves, such as the independence movements of Laothkund and Delthuntle.

## Maharaja

Maharaja (also spelled Maharajah) was a title used for positions of authority across a few different cultures, namely the Durpari of the Shining Lands and the outsiders known as marids and rakshasas.

Durpari Titles
The Kingdom of Durpar was originally founded under the rulership of a Maharajah, one by the name of Udandwi, in the . However, this authority would not remain forever. After Maharajah Waileen V passed away without an heir in, a high council comprised of Durpar's eleven richest nawabs (merchants) was convened to steward the kingdom until an heir could be pronounced. However, thirty years would pass, until finally the Nawab Council of Durpar was firmly cemented as the nation's governing body in 447 DR, united under the banner of the wealthiest among them, the Grand Nawab.

Rakshasa Titles
Within raksasha society, Maharajah was a title roughly analogous to what some on the Prime Material would call a "duke". Maharajahs were the unquestioned leaders of several small interrelated clans, or sometimes singular massive clans, composed of hundreds of members. Some were known to serve under even more dangerous entities and would leave a rajah to rule in their absence.

Befitting beings of deception, early reports on rakshasa society contradicted later descriptions, although both were based on subservience and subjugation and it was possible some combination of the two was present. Earlier claims were that rakshasas belonged to a unshakable caste system and that individuals were incapable of rising through the ranks. Later descriptions portrayed it as a meritocracy based on guile and ruthless immorality, where rakshasas constantly waged conspiratorial wars against each other. Enslavement, whether of rakshasa or some other creature, was an indication of one's power and their political battles ended either in the death or domination of the loser. In order to rise to the rank of Maharajah, one needed to successfully dominate over all other rakshasas in an area.

On the plane of Acheron, one Maharajah ruled over all raksashas who dwelt there. The raksashas of Acheron would often kidnap petitioners and planewalkers to serve as slaves in their palaces, hoping to impress the Maharajah. And a mysterious town in the divine realm of Merratet was rumored to be ruled over by a Maharajah.

Trivia
 The Great Padisha of the Marid was sometimes referred to as the "Maharajah of the Oceans".
 At some point the criminal organization known as the Night Masks divided their members up into three cadres, each entitled after a particular monarchical title. These were the Deys of Night, the Sultans of Sunset, and the Midnight Maharajas.

## Marid States

The Marid States was a realm or group of realms that was a great power of Serôs for over a thousand years, ruled by marids and janni originating from the Calim Empire.

Geography
The States were based in the depths below the Hmur Plateau, and largely spread throughout the deeper reaches of the surrounding waters were shallow-dwellers could not reach.

History
Around  a number of marids and janni rebelled and fled the Calim Empire, splashing into the Vilhon Reach and the underwater Selmalyr, causing a brief conflict with the native sea elves. Within the year they traveled into wider Serôs, settling in the depths below the Hmur Plateau beyond the reach of their neighbors. They proceeded to expand in the harder to reach depths of the sea, formed diplomatic ties with many realms and taught magic to their allies, becoming a dominant power in Serôs. In a similar move shortly after, the marid Ajhuu rebelled from Calim and founded the Maridlands in the eastern empire.

Peace accords between Aryselmalyr and the States ended their long-running conflicts in, and some janni joined the Dukar orders.

The Marid States came to an end in  when the majority of the marids and janni either vanished or were killed by krakens. The remainder continued to disappear over the following sixteen years, leaving Aryselmalyr as the dominant power of Serôs.The mass disappearance taking place the same year as the Calimemnon Crystal implies that the one-time vassals of Calim may have been imprisoned along with their former master.

## Mantle of atropal essence

The mantle of atropal essence was an artifact cloak that was imbued with the unholy power of the destroyed atropal that fueled the Soulmonger in the late 15 century DR.

Powers
The cloak granted its unholy power to anyone who wore it, boosting the wearer's vitality, dexterity, combat prowess, and the ability of their attacks, both physical and magical, to pierce enemy armor. Additionally, it increased the wearer's constitution. Lastly, the mantle of atropal essence was a part of a set, alongside the cincture of atropal essence and the decanter of atropal essence. When these artifacts were worn together, they imbued the wearer with great vitality every time the wearer received healing.

History
In the late 15 century DR, demilich Acererak used an atropal to power his Soulmonger that spread the death curse across Faerûn. When a group of adventurers slew the unholy atropal, the cincture of atropal essence, the mantle of atropal essence, and the decanter of atropal essence were pulled out of the pool that was formed out of the atropal's remnants.

## Master alchemist

Master alchemists were powerful arcane or divine spellcasters who were able to reproduce the effects of spells of  the 4 circle or higher using potions. They were the most adept among all alchemists.

Abilities
The most powerful master alchemists could replicate the effects of spells of even the 9 circle using specially prepared potions. However, this required the right raw materials, equipment, and sometimes even a whole alchemical lab. Aside from that, they could also cast spells conventionally like clerics or wizards.

They had an easier time further developing their alchemical skills. Additionally they were adept at developing their ability to concentrate, craft, and scry, as well as their spellcraft and arcane knowledge.

More powerful master alchemists had great knowledge about magical items and could identify them easily.

## Many Long Arms

The Many Long Arms was a band of thieves, spies, and other criminals that served the Rundeen mercantile organization in the mid-to-late 14 century DR and active in the Shining Sea region.

Organization
Effectively a private thieves' guild serving the Rundeen, they were controlled directly by the First Yrshelem, the second tier of Rundeen leadership, but technically ranked below the Mitalibbar, their collectors and watchers, like their other subsidiaries.

The actual leader of the Many Long Arms around 1370 DR was a masked man known as el Chaddalk; only the Yrshelem knew his true identity. He was aided by his vizar, Harun yn Riikaln, the Scarlet Sorcerer.

Members were typically dispatched on missions in threes or fours, so they operated similarly to many adventuring companies without actually being one.

Membership
True to their name, the Many Long Arms were a vast organization, the biggest of its kind south of Tethyr and second in size only to the Shadow Thieves of Amn. Their ranks included rogues, thieves, housebreakers, goons, smugglers, and even assassins and pirates. They were required to give a 35% cut of their 'earnings' to the organization. In return, they had use of safehouses, fences, moneychangers, and new false identities when required.

Activities
On behalf of the Rundeen, the Many Long Arms stole goods, framed rivals, and collected intelligence. It was said that if the Rundeen required information on any locale under  from the shore of the Shining Sea, then el Chaddalk would have it for them before the month was out. Their agents infiltrated almost every ship on the Shining Sea to acquire information or other peoples' goods.

Base of Operations
Again true to their name, the Many Long Arms had a huge reach thanks to their extensive network of agents. Their heartland was the Chultan Peninsula, but they reached across the Shining Sea to northern Calimshan, which was the origin of their name, and from there they could send agents further north. They were primarily dominant in Almraiven and Teshburl in Calimshan, with limited presences in Memnon and in Derlusk and Yallasch in the Border Kingdoms. They had many other agents in all other Shining Sea ports, but these ones were more independent and only reported in once a year.

Relationships
The Many Long Arms were one of a number of mercenary and adventuring bands, along with the Clenched Fist and Fist of Rundeen, formed by the Rundeen with the express purpose of opposing the Harpers.

Although almost as large as the Shadow Thieves, the Many Long Arms were more discreet and little-known. Few folk even knew of their existence outside the Rundeen and their enemies.

History
Within four hours of the death of Pasha Pook in the, the Many Long Arms brazenly looted his grand villa, Pook's Palace in Calimport. The twenty thieves simply sneaked around in the background, overlooked by panicking guards and distressed family and all, taking away absolutely everything of any value.

They had several clashes with the Harpers, but were defeated several times by them, who saw them as no longer effective by 1367 DR.
